  - text: "Always check README.md file for instructions how to build the project."
  - text: "Always build and test before you move to the next step."
  - text: "Always use ".\build.bat build" to compile the project."
  - text: "Always use ".\build.bat run" to execute the project."
  - text: "Always use ".\build.bat clean" to clean the project."
  - text: "Always use ".\build.bat all" to clean and compile and run the project."
  - text: |
      # Coding Standards, Domain Knowledge, and Preferences
      - This is a real-time, interactive 3D flocking simulation using modern OpenGL (3.3+) and Qt (5 or 6).
      - The system models collective behavior of autonomous agents ("boids") using classic flocking algorithms.
      - Focus is on modularity, extensibility, and real-time performance.
      - Use modern C++ best practices (C++11 or later):
        - Prefer smart pointers over raw pointers.
        - Use const correctness and references where appropriate.
        - Prefer range-based for loops and STL containers.
        - Use RAII for resource management.
      - Follow modular architecture: keep simulation, rendering, and UI logic separated.
      - Use clear, descriptive naming for classes, functions, and variables.
      - Document non-obvious code with comments, especially for algorithms and UI logic.
      - Use OpenGL and Qt idioms for graphics and UI code.
      - Prefer header/source file separation for C++ code.
      - Use `#pragma once` in all header files.
      - Use vcpkg for dependency management (recommended) or Chocolatey for Windows.
      - Dependencies: Qt 5/6, OpenGL 3.3+, glad2 (included as source), GLM.
      - MinGW is recommended for Windows builds; CMake is supported if CMakeLists.txt is present.
      - Build using `mingw32-make` or `build.bat` (Windows), or CMake if available.
      - The main window provides controls for simulation parameters, rendering options, and obstacle properties.
      - UI should allow real-time adjustment of flock size, boid/obstacle appearance, and simulation dynamics.
      - Keyboard shortcuts and additional controls should be documented in the UI or code comments.
      - Use performance monitoring and validation tools provided in the codebase.
      - Optimize for real-time rendering and simulation.
      - The boid concept and flocking algorithm are based on Craig Reynolds' work.
      - Project is for educational and research purposes. See LICENSE for details.
      - Acknowledge original and additional contributors in code and documentation.
